Change has been successfully rebased and submitted as 8c9db69c98aa9ccc132483d28083556f63c128e9
Should/can we add support to deserialize from JSON also?  I think it would be good if we can make a transition from Cereal to JSON, eventually disabling Cereal via a meson option.
Done
I had to look up what this "version" was but it looks like a BMC version and not a structure version.  Do we need some kind of versioning on the JSON structure itself?
Done - Added a new field called `jsonVersion `which will keep track of the json structure version

Since this function is only used for testing it isn't a big deal, but if JSON were to ever replace cereal, we'd want to do everything we can to keep an event log if the version is newer than the latest the code understands so that we can support code downgrades without losing event logs.
From what I remember the [] operator will just crash if the key isn't found, but the at() operator will throw.  So I think at() would be better here.
I have now replaced [] with .at() for accessing individual fields

Why did we chose a floating point for a version number?
```suggestion
static constexpr size_t JSON_FORMAT_VERSION = 1.0;
```
Done
What are we doing if the json version is less than the expected?
Added a placeholder for upgrading it to the newer version, by setting the newer fields in the if block and always reading the fields existing in the older version outside if.

I would suggest doing this in the same order as the cereal `load` function.  It is a lot easier to review and compare that way.

That means moving resolved up here.
Done
Is there a reason we're renaming the entire directory due to a single corrupted file?  If so, can we leave a comment here as to why?
path - points to single entry file, it is renaming that file and saving under the parent directory overwriting any existing file, same as existing logic in deserialize

Can we add test cases that attempts to deserialize:
1. a corrupted JSON
2. a JSON missing a field.

We should confirm that the result is the expected exception.
Done
sorry, I missed this before, can you change this to serializeJSON since JSON is an acronym?  same with function below.
Done
